page.overview:
Who is Manny Ayulo?

Manny began in hot rods and midget cars in California after WWII. He entered the AAA Championship Car series in 1948, competing in 44 races over eight seasons. He was runner-up in the national standings in 1954, claiming two wins (Darlington & Milwaukee) and three second-place finishes.

With the Indy 500 included in the F1 World Championship from 1950 to 1960, Ayulo appeared in six Grand Prix entries (with four starts) across the years 1950–1955.

On May 16, 1955, during a late-evening practice run for the Indianapolis 500, Ayulo crashed head-on into a concrete wall at approximately 140 mph. Investigators suggested possible fatigue and steering failure. He was not wearing a seatbelt, and his pockets held tools that may have compounded his injuries. He died from a basal skull fracture on May 17, 1955.
